name: rally-1882c5f6-blind30-ots
instr:
# rally-regen

A tool that drives performance benchmarks against a search cluster now misbehaves almost everywhere we point it, from the moment we launch it to the closing summary, and nothing in the history explains any of it. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the cluster changed and nothing about the way we invoke the tool changed. What follows is only what we could see from the outside.

What we type before anything starts is already answered wrongly. On the oldest interpreter the tool says it supports, launching aborts complaining the interpreter is too old and must be upgraded, while a newer one launches fine. When the tool declines to run inside a container because the chosen pipeline is not the benchmark-only one, the online help web address printed with the refusal is mangled: the page name has swallowed the site prefix instead of being appended to it. Asking which is the lowest cluster build we may benchmark against hands back the number with the trailing newline of the file it came from still attached, so it never compares equal to the plain number written there. In a comma-separated settings string, a value in quotation marks loses its first character: a certificate location given in quotes arrives without its leading slash, and a quoted one-character value arrives empty, while unquoted numbers, booleans and null-like words behave as before. Asking for a ceiling on how many sockets may be open at once yields one more than ask
